title: Requirements
intro: Four stories are settled. Write the fifth, the one a member asked for, with criteria a tester could check.
taskPanel:
# Requirements: write the missing story

The shelf's backlog has four settled stories. A member has asked for a fifth:
to see which of an author's books are free to borrow right now. Write SH-5 in
the story form in this room; it is saved as `requirements/story.json`.

## What good looks like

- One story in the *As a … I want … so that …* form, naming who wants it and why.
- At least two acceptance criteria in the *Given … When … Then …* form: tag one
  happy path and one boundary, the book that is already on loan.
- At least one thing the story leaves out of scope.

## Using the AI mentor well

Ask the mentor to question your story, not to write it: "what would a tester
ask about this criterion?" gets you further than "write SH-5".
objectives: Write SH-5 in the As a / I want / so that form
Give it at least two Given / When / Then acceptance criteria
Cover the case of a book that is already on loan

criteria.title: Story
criteria.description: Who wants it, what they want, and why.

criteria.title: Acceptance criteria
criteria.description: Given / When / Then criteria a tester could check, including a book on loan.

criteria.title: Completeness
criteria.description: Enough criteria and scope lines to say what is in and what is left out.

providedStories.title: Browse the shelf
providedStories.capability: to see every book in shelf order
providedStories.benefit: I can find one without asking

criteria.when: I filter by an author in any case
criteria.then: only that author's books are listed

providedStories.title: Lend a book
providedStories.capability: to record who has borrowed a book

criteria.when: I lend it to a member
criteria.then: the book says who has it

criteria.when: I try to lend it again

providedStories.title: Return a book
providedStories.capability: to put a returned book back
providedStories.benefit: the next member can borrow it

criteria.then: it is on the shelf again
the request is refused as not found

providedStories.title: See what is out
providedStories.capability: the shelf to say which books are on loan
providedStories.benefit: I do not walk to an empty space

assistant.systemPrompt: You are the LearnSDLC mentor for the REQUIREMENTS phase of Shelf, a teacher's own application: a Python Flask API that keeps books in memory and a TypeScript React page that lists them. The learner writes story SH-5 in the Requirements room's story form, saved as requirements/story.json. Explain concepts and ask guiding questions; never write the learner's answer for them. Keep replies under 120 words and end with one question.

hints: Who is asking for this, and what would they do differently once they had it?
Read SH-1 to SH-4: which part of each sentence names the reason?
What state is the shelf in before the member acts, and what can a tester observe afterwards?
Could someone who never met you decide pass or fail from your criterion alone?
What should a member see for an author whose only book is out?
Is 'free to borrow' the same as 'on the shelf'? Which story already says what on loan means?

progressive: Start with the sentence: who, what, and why.
Then the criteria: one ordinary case and one about a book already on loan.
Read each criterion as a tester would: could you check it without asking you?
